findings.text: Persistent memory security fixes passphrase storage at 32 bytes and key descriptor storage at 22 bytes.
Key material is a fixed byte array sized by the passphrase length. Passphrase role distinguishes a user credential from a master credential.

A DIMM provider offers a security vector that reports flag bits for a chosen role and requests freeze, key rotation with old and new material, unlock, disable, role scoped erase, overwrite, overwrite status, and master disable. Queries return bit state while mutations report success or failure.
DIMM security occupies one of disabled, unlocked, locked, frozen, or overwrite conditions. Flag and key operations are qualified by user versus master role.

Firmware activation has a device state of invalid, idle, armed, busy, or arm overflow. A trigger arms or disarms. Capability reports invalid, none, quiesce, or live. Result reports invalid, none, success, not staged, need reset, or fail.
Firmware activation is split into a bus vector for state query, capability query, and activation, and a device vector for state query, result query, and arm or disarm with a trigger value.

DIMM creation accepts bus, provider data, attribute groups, flags, command mask, and flush resources and forwards them with empty optional callbacks to the core creator. DIMM control resolves the owning bus and descriptor from the DIMM and delegates the command with buffer and status pointer to the descriptor handler.

Persistent memory mapping has two build variants. One selects write back mapping. The other selects write through mapping and provides empty cache write back and invalidate helpers that accept address and length and do nothing.

License compatibility is an exact string match predicate. It accepts plain, versioned, additional rights, and three dual license wordings covering BSD, MIT, and MPL combinations, and rejects all other labels.

Size and address maxima use all bits set, with signed maxima at half range and signed minima as negated maxima minus one. Unsigned minima are zero. This pattern covers machine word, physical address, resource, and 8, 16, 32, and 64 bit widths.

A linear range maps selector values to measured values with a minimum value, minimum selector, maximum selector, and step. Initializer helpers build an entry from those four fields and an indexed array entry from index plus the same fields.
C linkage for assembly entry points uses extern C under C++ and empty otherwise, exposed through a common linkage marker. A protection helper for that marker is a no operation loop.

Page aligned data and bss request section placement plus page size alignment, with assembly section forms and a page table bss alias. Symbol construction separates type for function, object, and none, binding for global, weak, and local, and alignment choice, with function alignment driven by configuration.

Syscall compatibility helpers provide a weak default binding to the not implemented handler and a global alias binding between two names. Legacy wrappers map global definition, function entry, weak entry, size close, and procedure close onto the newer symbol primitives.

Generic symbol primitives emit a labeled entry with chosen binding and alignment, close a symbol with type and computed size, define an alias to an existing name, and define inner labels with or without alignment and untyped type.

Function, code, and data helpers specialize the generic primitives by binding and alignment. Functions cover global, local, and weak starts with aligned or unaligned forms plus typed close and global, local, and weak aliases. Code covers global and local starts with aligned or unaligned forms plus untyped close. Data covers global and local starts, typed close, labeled end, and whole definition helpers.
Live patch transition state is idle at negative one, unpatched at zero, and patched at one.

A patched function descriptor carries old name, replacement pointer, and optional duplicate symbol position, plus resolved old address, old and new sizes, kernel object, list and stack membership, and flags for no operation, patched, and transition.

A patch object groups a target name, static function array, and callbacks with kernel object, function list, node linkage, module, and dynamic and patched flags. State carries identifier, version, and data pointer. A patch groups module, static objects, static states, and replace flag with list linkage, kernel object, object list, enabled and forced flags, deferred free work, and completion.
Static iteration walks null terminated arrays using presence of name or function data as continuation, while live iteration walks kernel lists with plain and safe forms for objects and functions.
Shadow object support defines a constructor taking object and shadow data returning status and a destructor taking object and shadow data returning nothing.

With live patch enabled, pending query reflects a per task thread flag and reliable stack requires both stack trace and reliable stack trace support. With it disabled, module notification, pending query, patch state update, and process copy hooks are inert with false or zero results.
A fallback relocation applier accepts module, section headers, string tables, symbol and section indexes, and object name and reports success without acting.

External live patch uses distinct dotted prefixes for relocation sections and symbol references, and distinct callback symbol bases for pre patch, post patch, pre unpatch, and post unpatch in both raw and stringified forms.

External callbacks group pre and post patch plus pre and post unpatch function pointers and a post unpatch enable flag. External function and object descriptors carry names, replacement pointers, symbol position or count, and callbacks, with pre patch reporting status and the other three returning nothing.

Scheduler assisted switch is attempted only when a dedicated static branch is enabled and the current task state includes freezable, otherwise it does nothing. A disabled build provides an empty helper with the same task parameter.

Live update file handling centers on an argument bundle of handler, retrieve status, file, serialized data, and private data. The operation vector covers preservation test, preserve, unpreserve, freeze, unfreeze, retrieve, finish test, finish, identifier query, and owner. A handler pairs that vector with a compatibility string and private global and dependency list links.

A fresnel block pairs an operation vector and compatibility string with private state. Arguments carry block, scalar data, and object pointer. Operations cover preserve, unpreserve, retrieve, and finish plus owner. Private state tracks reference count, data, object, finished flag, and retrieve status under a mutex, duplicated for outgoing and incoming directions with user count and initialization flag.

With live update disabled, enablement reports false and reboot reports success. Registration and incoming or outgoing acquisition report not supported, while unregistration and release helpers do nothing.

Logical IO memory access is a vector of offset and size qualified read, write, fill, copy out, and copy in plus an unmap release, each with opaque private context. Region mapping resolves an offset and length to that vector and context and reports status.

Fresnel block direction state serializes concurrent preserve, retrieve, and finish transitions with a mutex and reference count; finished and status fields are meaningful only under that protection. Handler and block list membership implies external registration locking not shown here.

Callers must honor fixed passphrase sizing, frozen versus locked DIMM behavior, firmware arm overflow and need reset outcomes, duplicate live patch symbol positions, and disabled live update or live patch fallbacks that silently succeed or report unsupported without acting.
Task pending query depends on an external thread flag test owned elsewhere.
Scheduler switch gating depends on an external static branch test owned elsewhere.
Scheduler switch gating has an alternate external static branch test form owned elsewhere.
Scheduler task state sampling depends on an external one shot read accessor owned elsewhere.
